termag: manage termag boxes and projects from the command line.

Commands:
  tui                  Open the terminal UI: your projects, live status, peek and attach
  login                Sign this device in through the browser
  logout               Sign this device out and revoke its token
  whoami               Show the signed-in user and the orchestrator
  doctor               Check this machine's termag setup and offer to fix what is missing
  box list             List your boxes
  project list         List your projects as <box>/<project>
  box create           Create a box; --size small (2 vCPU, 8 GB), medium (4, 16) or large (4, 32), else your default size; --disk 50 to 300 GB, else 120; --minimal for the lean image; --no-setup to turn termag setup off
  box start            Start a stopped box; its projects come back on their own
  box stop             Stop a box, keeping its disk and projects; a box running Claude Code cloud sessions needs --force, which ends them
  box keep             Keep a running box up: restart its idle clock, as using it would, so auto-park waits another full limit
  box set              Change box settings: --auto-park parks it after that long idle, --terminate-after terminates it after that long parked
  box rename           Rename a box; its projects stay on it, now named <new-name>/<project>
  box resize           Resize a box to small (2 vCPU, 8 GB), medium (4, 16) or large (4, 32): it stops for two to three minutes, and running turns stop with it; a stopped or hibernated box is resized and left stopped. --disk grows its disk (up to 300 GB, never smaller, once every six hours) with the box up
  box rm               Terminate a box and archive its projects
  project create       Create a project on a box, or on a new box with --new-box (at --size, else the repository's or environment's or your default size)
  project rename       Rename a project; it stays on the same box
  project archive      Archive a project
  ssh                  Open a shell on a box or in a project's directory, or run a command there
  attach               Attach this terminal to a project's agent session (--ctrl: its ctrl shell)
  ssh-config           Print, or with --install add, the `Host termag-*` entry for ~/.ssh/config
  ssh-proxy            The ssh-config entry's ProxyCommand (run by ssh, not by hand)
  forward              Forward local ports to ports on a box through the orchestrator, until Ctrl-C
  preview publish      Publish a port of a workstream's box at https://<name>.<preview domain>
  preview list         List your live preview links, or a project's links and pending requests
  preview revoke       Revoke one of your preview links by its name
  preview run          Run a dev server confined to this checkout, so a preview link of it can be shared beyond you
  preview request      Ask the box's owner to share a port as a preview link (for agents on a box)
  ask                  Ask another project's agent; prints its answer and a draft PR for any commits (a --thread follow-up while it works joins the running turn)
  space ls             List the spaces you (or this box) can reach, or the files in one
  space get            Download a file, or a folder with -r
  space url            Print a browser link to a file; it opens for anyone who can read the space, or everyone on termag once shared
  space share          Share a file read-only with everyone signed in to termag (needs editor or owner)
  space unshare        Make a shared file private again: only the space's members can open it
  space put            Upload a file, or a folder with -r; refused (exit 6) if it changed since you read it
  space rm             Delete a file, or a folder with -r (old versions are kept); a file you read is checked first
  space mv             Move or rename a file or folder (folders end in /); a file you read is checked first
  space create         Create a space; you become its owner
  space members        List or change a space's members
  space boxes          List or change the boxes that can reach a space
  space slack          Link Slack channels to a space, and manage its Slack (owners); not `space link`, which is `space url`
  space memory         Load and change a space's shared agent memory (.termag/)
  space sync           Copy the spaces you (or this box) reach to ~/termag/spaces, read-only
  handoff              Hand an agent off: it writes a handoff, then its context is cleared or compacted, or the pane restarts, and the next agent starts on it
  automation list      List your automations, with their schedule, state and next run
  automation create    Create an automation: a project whose prompt a fresh agent runs on a schedule; --preview shows the next runs and creates nothing
  automation show      Show an automation: its schedule, space folder, next runs and last runs with their state
  automation edit      Change an automation's schedule, prompt, name, space or settings; any change clears a pause
  automation pause     Pause an automation: no scheduled runs until it is resumed (Run now still works)
  automation resume    Resume a paused automation, from its next occurrence (missed ones are not owed)
  automation run       Run an automation now, as its Run now button does
  automation stop      Stop a live run of an automation
  automation rm        Delete an automation: its project is archived and its runs stop; the run history stays
  bug report           Report a termag bug: a termag command or feature that behaved wrongly
  bug list             List termag bug reports, new first (admins, on their own box)
  bug show             Show one termag bug report with its history (admins, on their own box)
  bug triage           Triage a termag bug report: status, duplicate, link, note (admins, on their own box)
  feedback             Log feedback about termag that a person gave: praise, a problem, an idea
  environment list     List your personal environments, then the shared ones (anyone can use those; admins change them)
  environment show     Show an environment: its definition or pointer, and the repositories it resolves to now
  environment create   Create an environment from a definition (JSON, checked against docs/environment.schema.json) or a pointer to a file
  environment edit     Replace an environment's definition or pointer (every change is in its history; a shared one: admins only)
  environment share    Share your environment with everyone (admins only): it must point at a file on its repository's default branch
  environment unshare  Make a shared environment personal again, its owner's alone (admins only)
  environment history  An environment's history: every change, who made it and when, newest first
  environment delete   Delete an environment, a shared one for everyone and by an admin (its history stays; projects made from it keep their repositories)
  events               Stream your boxes' state changes and your agents' status changes, until Ctrl-C
  update               Pull the termag checkout this CLI was installed from and reinstall it

Global flags:
  --json          Machine-readable output
  --yes           Skip confirmations
  --host <url>    Orchestrator to use (or TERMAG_URL). Default: the production orchestrator,
                  or this box's own orchestrator when run on a box
  -h, --help      Show help
  --version       Show the version

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage error, 3 not found, 4 auth needed, 5 timeout.
